sections.title: Lifestyle Allocation
sections.body: Your wardrobe should mirror how you actually spend your dressed hours, not an idealized version of your life. The tops×bottoms×shoes combinatorics formula is the key diagnostic — a few high-versatility neutrals beat many low-versatility statement pieces, because the math is multiplicative.

sections.title: The Formality Spectrum
sections.body: Business casual has real internal sub-tiers, from 'startup casual' (jacket optional) to 'boardroom casual' (structured layer expected). Your GCC baseline sits lower-to-middle on that scale — but near-daily leadership visibility means keeping an escalation register genuinely ready, not just occasionally available.

sections.title: Colour Theory
sections.body: 12-season analysis is a narrowing heuristic, not a verdict — especially from photos with unknown white balance. Your own read is genuinely split between Deep Winter (validated by your loved emerald/purple) and Deep Autumn (validated by your best-lit photo). A real daylight swatch test settles it faster than more photo analysis.

sections.title: Fit & Proportion
sections.body: At 172cm, standard Western-block sizing systematically over-sizes: shoulder overhang, excess sleeve/jacket length, low rise, full break. None of this is about disguising height — it's the same precision-fit logic a 190cm man needs in the opposite direction.

sections.title: The Bangalore Climate Constraint
sections.body: No real winter means the four-season Western wardrobe model doesn't apply. The real design problem is the AC-swing — hot humid commute, cold office — solved with a decoupled layer (an overshirt kept at the desk), not one fabric weight trying to do both jobs.
